subject: Stonebridge RFP — Legal governance & liability alignment
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@stonebridgehealth.com>, procurement@stonebridgehealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Stonebridge RFP — Legal governance & liability alignment

Hi Erin / Stonebridge procurement team,

Attached are Redwood's initial responses to the legal questionnaire and a draft order form highlighting our proposed positions on IP, indemnity, liability caps, and data residency. Key points upfront:

- IP: Redwood will not assign underlying model IP; we offer output rights for customer use as described in the questionnaire.
- Indemnity: We can indemnify for Redwood-provided services to the extent of our negligence or willful misconduct; we cannot accept broad customer-side indemnities (e.g., claims arising from customer-supplied data or customer modifications).
- Liability cap: We propose an overall liability cap tied to the greater of 3x annual fees or $5,000,000, with carveouts for willful misconduct and IP infringement.
- Data residency & security: SOC 2 Type II report available; we support VPC/private deployments for regulated data.

Please find: redwood_rfp_legal_qs_answers_v1.pdf and proposed-order-form-draft.docx attached.

We'd like to align on any high-priority redlines before the legal call. Are you available for a 30-minute call Tue May 20 at 11:00 AM ET?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference platform

From: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@stonebridgehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, procurement@stonebridgehealth.com
Cc: Mark Dunn <mdunn@stonebridgehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 May 2025 10:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Stonebridge RFP — Legal governance & liability alignment

Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. We circulated the draft with our legal team and Mark has marked several items that require clarification or a counterproposal. Summary of Stonebridge positions that drove the redlines:

1) Indemnity carveouts: We need Redwood to accept indemnity for third-party claims of IP infringement where the claim arises from Redwood's models or service (not for customer-supplied data or customer prompts).
2) Liability cap: Our procurement policy limits liability caps but allows higher limits for critical vendors. We are open to a tiered approach (e.g., standard cap + higher cap for breach-of-confidentiality/data-exfiltration).
3) Data residency & audit rights: We require audit evidence (SOC2 report + evidence of logging/audit trails) and an option for on-prem or VPC deployment for PHI.

I've attached our redlines (stonebridge_redlines_marked.docx) and included inline notes. A few specific asks: can Redwood accept an IP infringement indemnity limited to instances directly caused by Redwood's code or trained models (not downstream prompt content)? Can you provide an explicit audit-log SLA and evidence of encryption-at-rest + KMS options?

The team is available for Tue May 20 at 11:00 AM ET — that works for us. Please confirm call attendees and any pre-read you want us to focus on.

Best,
Erin Walsh
Senior Procurement Manager, Stonebridge Health
erin.walsh@stonebridgehealth.com

Attachment: stonebridge_redlines_marked.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 May 2025 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Stonebridge redlines — quick internal take

Jordan / Kimberly — quick internal note before we reply to Stonebridge:

- IP indemnity: We can accept indemnity limited to claims arising from Redwood's delivery (e.g., our code, the hosted model artifacts we provide). We will not indemnify for customer prompts or customer-provided training data.
- Liability cap: Propose the following structure: general cap = the greater of (3x annually recurring fees) or $5M; elevated cap for security incidents impacting customer data = up to $10M (or a mutually agreed fixed number) but only for verified breaches caused by Redwood.
- Carveouts: No cap for willful misconduct and proven IP infringement; also carve out obligations to comply with subpoenas where appropriate.

I put a short table together (redwood_proposal_table.xlsx). For the call, Kimberly should bring SOC2 summary and KMS details; Jordan will own the commercial framing.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@stonebridgehealth.com>, procurement@stonebridgehealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stonebridge RFP — Legal governance & liability alignment

Erin / Mark — thanks for the redlines. After internal review, Redwood can accept a narrowed IP indemnity limited to claims arising from Redwood-developed code and model artifacts that we supply as part of the service. We will explicitly exclude claims that flow from customer-supplied data, customer prompts, or customer modifications.

Liability cap — proposed compromise language below (snippets attached):

- "Aggregate liability of Redwood arising out of or relating to the Agreement shall be limited to the greater of (a) three times the fees paid or payable by Customer to Redwood in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, or (b) five million US dollars (US $5,000,000)."
- "Notwithstanding the foregoing, for verified security incidents resulting in unauthorized access to Customer data attributable to Redwood, Redwood's aggregate liability shall be capped at ten million US dollars (US $10,000,000)."
- Carveouts: liability shall not be limited for claims arising from Redwood's willful misconduct or proven IP infringement where Redwood is adjudicated as the infringer.

We can also provide an audit-log SLA and SOC2 Type II summary as pre-read. See attached compromise_clause_snippets.txt.

Call Tue May 20, 11:00 AM ET — confirmed. Attendees from our side: Jordan Blake (Enterprise), Ben Carter (Head of Contracts), Kimberly Park (Security & Compliance). Please send a calendar invite and any additional pre-reads you want the legal team to see.

Regards,
Jordan

From: Mark Dunn <mdunn@stonebridgehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@stonebridgehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 20:10:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Stonebridge RFP — Legal governance & liability alignment

Jordan / Erin — thanks for the proposed language. High-level feedback from our legal team:

- The IP indemnity carve (limited to Redwood-provided models/artifacts) is reasonable, but we will need more detail on your model provenance and any third-party model licenses used.
- The tiered liability cap is acceptable in principle; we will ask procurement for written justification for the $10M elevated cap for data incidents.
- Auditability: Stonebridge requires (1) a SOC2 Type II report covering Redwood's service, (2) confirmation of encryption at rest and in transit, and (3) evidence that KMS-driven key separation is available for enterprise accounts. Also include a short description of logging retention and ability to produce exportable audit logs for review.

I've attached our vendor-security-reqs.xlsx with the items we will verify during due diligence. If you can circulate SOC2 summary and KMS notes ahead of the call, that will speed review.

-Mark Dunn
General Counsel, Stonebridge Health
mdunn@stonebridgehealth.com

Attachment: vendor-security-reqs.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Stonebridge RFP — Legal governance & liability alignment

Hi Mark / Erin — attaching the SOC2 Type II summary and KMS integration notes ahead of today's call (SOC2_type2_2024_summary.pdf; KMS-integration-notes.pdf). A few quick clarifications:

- SOC2: We have a completed Type II audit for 2024 covering the hosted inference runtime and control environment; we cannot share customer-specific evidence but can provide the attest report under NDA.
- Encryption & KMS: Encryption at rest and in transit is standard. For enterprise customers we offer dedicated KMS key support (bring-your-own-key) for session keys and control-plane access.
- Audit logs: Logs are retained for 90 days by default; extended retention (up to 2 years) and exportable audit artifacts can be provided under dedicated deployment agreements.
- Data residency: See attached data-residency-Annex.docx for our typical options (multi-region hosted vs VPC/private deployment).

We look forward to the 11:00 AM ET call — joining from Redwood: Jordan Blake, Ben Carter, and I.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachments: SOC2_type2_2024_summary.pdf; KMS-integration-notes.pdf; data-residency-Annex.docx
